items.summary: fix: finish A2A tasks for messages sent while the agent is still answering (#200846) Root cause: `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts:165` completes an A2A task only when dispatch returns `deferredToActiveRun` unset, and #183803 settles only `"followup"` later through `onQueuedFollowupReplyBatch`; a `"steer"` result has no reply delivery or queued batch of its own, so nothing ever settles that task. Fixes #200646 ## What Problem This Solves With the default `steer` queue mode, an A2A peer that sends a second message while the first is still being answered gets a new task for it. The agent answers that message inside the running turn, but the new task stays `TASK_STATE_WORKING` forever, so a peer polling `GetTask` waits indefinitely and never sees the answer. ## User Impact A2A peers now get a terminal state for every message steered into an active turn: `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with the replies the turn delivered after the message joined it, `TASK_STATE_FAILED` (`Agent run failed`) if that turn fails, or `TASK_STATE_FAILED` (`Agent run aborted`) if an operator stops it. These are the same states a queued followup gets. Tasks that start their own turn or queue as a followup are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The A2A dispatch whose run is executing in a session records the final replies it delivers. That is either its own run, or its queued followup's run once that starts: queued followups call the source dispatch's run-start observer. A dispatch that comes back as steered registers with that owner, and when the owner's run ends the steered task settles through the same settlement #183803 added for queued followups (same reply filtering, same `Agent run ` failure). A followup run ends with its terminal batch. Core reports a run's end as completed or failed and reports nothing for a cancelled run, so a run that reported neither settles its steered tasks as aborted. A followup that never starts never becomes the owner, so a dropped followup leaves nothing behind. No core, SDK, schema or config change. ## Evidence Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`, bundled `a2a` channel, `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`) with a local OpenAI-compatible provider fixture. An A2A peer sends m1 ("answer ONE", reply delayed 8 s), then m2 ("answer TWO") 2 s later in the same `contextId`, both with `returnImmediately`, and polls `GetTask` on both. - Base `f3638439b9` (twice): m1 `COMPLETED ["ONE"]`, m2 `WORKING []` 45 s after the turn ended. The fixture log shows m2 was answered (`TWO`) inside m1's run. - Candidate (twice): m1 `COMPLETED ["ONE"]`, m2 `COMPLETED` with an artifact holding the replies `ONE` and `TWO`, about 10 s after sending. - Failure control (provider returns 500 on every request): base m1 `FAILED`, m2 still `WORKING` 65 s later; candidate m1 and m2 both `FAILED` (`Agent run failed`). - Operator stop (`openclaw gateway call chat.abort`) after the run consumed the steer: base m2 still `WORKING` 60 s later (twice); previous head 4968ee20a3 m2 `COMPLETED` without text (the review finding); candidate m2 `FAILED` `Agent run aborted` (twice). Normal flow on the same build: m2 `COMPLETED` with `ONE` and `TWO`. - Built artifact (`ocx build --dts`, `node dist/entry.js`) at this head for the stop and normal runs. - Steered into a queued followup's run (start in `followup` mode so m2 queues, operator runs `openclaw config set messages.queue.mode steer` while m2's run executes, m3 then steers into it): base 8c09105a m3 still `WORKING` 60 s later (twice, plus once with an operator stop); candidate m3 `COMPLETED` with `TWO` and `THREE` (twice), or `FAILED` `Agent run aborted` when the operator stops the run (twice). - Full captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6963955920, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6964428507 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6965151308 - Regression tests: `settles a message steered into the active run when that run completes|fails|is cancelled` (red on base for all three; cancelled case red on 4968ee20a3) and `settles a message steered into a queued followup's run with that run's batch` (red on 8c09105a). `inbound.test.ts` + `http.test.ts` pass at this head (41/41). Thanks @alexph-dev for the precise report and probe. Merge danger: two-way door. The change is local to the A2A plugin's inbound dispatch and writes no new state; a revert restores the old behavior exactly. Blast radius: A2A peers only; other channels and the core queue are untouched. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
